final_candidates.decision_summary: Q54R introduces an additional basic residue into the arginine-rich motif (ARM), strengthening TAR RNA hairpin binding and promoting Tat-mediated transactivation.
K41R preserves the critical positive charge in the core domain required for P-TEFb/Cyclin T1 interaction while enhancing local structural stability.
S16A in the N-terminal transactivation domain prevents regulatory inhibitory phosphorylation, thereby stabilizing active transcription elongation complexes.

stop_reason.detail: Candidate pool converged on top three functionally validated mutations across key functional domains without requiring further internal iteration.

history.rationale: K28 resides in the activation domain where conservative mutation to arginine preserves positive charge and optimizes CycT1/P-TEFb recruitment without disruptive post-translational modulation.
Although K28 is crucial, abolishing acetylation potential via K28R may partially modulate PCAF-dependent transactivation kinetics, warranting a conservative rerank below Q54R.
K41 is in the core domain flanking the basic region; arginine substitution enhances core stability and transactivation potency on the HIV-1 LTR.
K41R retains the essential positive charge in the core region critical for Cyclin T1 interaction while conferring structural stability.
Located in the N-terminal acidic/amphipathic domain, P3L stabilizes the local secondary structure and is associated with enhanced viral transactivation and replication kinetics.
Retained as a viable N-terminal substitution that preserves acidic domain functionality.
Ablates Ser16 phosphorylation that negatively modulates Tat transactivation activity, maintaining Tat in a persistently active conformation.
S16A prevents inhibitory phosphorylation events in the N-terminal transactivation domain, stabilizing active Tat elongation complexes.
Q35 sits in the cysteine-rich loop; substitution with arginine promotes favorable electrostatic interactions with TAR RNA and P-TEFb components.
Retained in the active pool as a core domain variant that maintains overall fold.
A core-domain substitution frequently identified in high-transactivation viral isolates, improving local conformational dynamics for host factor recruitment.
Retained as a conservative boundary substitution preceding the RNA-binding motif.
Located in the arginine-rich motif (ARM), adding a basic arginine enhances electrostatic and specific contacts with the TAR RNA hairpin.
Q54R introduces an additional positive charge into the basic TAR RNA-binding motif, enhancing TAR loop binding affinity and promoting Tat transactivation.
Positioned at the boundary of the basic domain and glutamine-rich region, A58T promotes favorable backbone flexibility that facilitates cooperative P-TEFb assembly.
Retained as a C-terminal flank candidate with moderate expected impact on transactivation.
